nodes.summary: The axioms say which sort has which sort as its type: $\mathrm{Prop}$ has type $\mathrm{Type}_0$, and $\mathrm{Type}_i$ has type $\mathrm{Type}_{i+1}$ for every natural number $i$. No other pair of sorts is related.
nodes.title: Sort axioms of CCω

nodes.summary: No closed term has type $\Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$: there is no term $t$ with $\vdash t : \Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$ in the empty context.
nodes.title: Consistency of CCω

nodes.summary: Beta conversion is the equivalence closure of one-step beta reduction: every term is convertible to itself, and if $t$ is convertible to $u$ and $u$ reduces to $v$ in one step, or $v$ reduces to $u$ in one step, then $t$ is convertible to $v$.
nodes.title: Beta conversion

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $c$, shifting a term $t$ by $d$ above the cutoff $c$ adds $d$ to every variable index $i \ge c$ and leaves every index $i < c$ unchanged. The cutoff goes up by one under each binder, that is, in the body of a $\lambda$ and in the codomain of a $\Pi$ (not in the type annotation or the domain), and sorts are unchanged. Thus the free variables of $t$ with index at least $c$ are increased by…
nodes.title: Shifting de Bruijn indices

nodes.summary: The product rules say in which sort $s_3$ a dependent product $\Pi (x : A).\, B$ lives when $A$ lives in the sort $s_1$ and $B$ lives in the sort $s_2$. There are exactly three rules: for every sort $s$, a product with domain in $s$ and codomain in $\mathrm{Prop}$ lives in $\mathrm{Prop}$ (the impredicativity of $\mathrm{Prop}$); for all natural numbers $i$ and $j$, a product with domain in $\mathrm{Type}_i$ and…
nodes.title: Product rules of CCω

nodes.summary: The strongly normalizing terms are defined inductively: a term $t$ is strongly normalizing when every term to which $t$ reduces in one beta step is strongly normalizing. Equivalently, classically, there is no infinite chain of one-step beta reductions starting from $t$.
nodes.title: Strongly normalizing terms

nodes.summary: The sorts are $\mathrm{Prop}$ and $\mathrm{Type}_i$ for every natural number $i$. In the calculus, $\mathrm{Prop}$ is impredicative and the $\mathrm{Type}_i$ form a predicative hierarchy.
nodes.title: Sorts of CCω

nodes.summary: The polymorphic identity $\lambda (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \lambda (x : A).\, x$ applied to $\bot = \Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$ reduces in one beta step to $\lambda (x : \bot).\, x$.
nodes.title: Beta step of the applied polymorphic identity

nodes.summary: One-step beta reduction is the smallest relation on terms that contains every beta step $(\lambda (x : A).\, b)\, a \to b[a/x]$, where $b[a/x]$ substitutes $a$ for the bound variable $x$ in $b$, and that is closed under every term former: a step inside the function or the argument of an application, inside the type annotation or the body of a $\lambda$, or inside the domain or the codomain of a $\Pi$ is a step of…
nodes.title: One-step beta reduction

nodes.summary: Every well-typed term is strongly normalizing: if $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ for some context $\Gamma$ and some term $A$, then $t$ is strongly normalizing.
nodes.title: Strong normalization of CCω

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a context and $t$, $t'$, $A$ terms of the calculus of constructions with universes. If $t$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$, that is $\Gamma \vdash t : A$, and $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one step of beta reduction (anywhere inside $t$), then $\Gamma \vdash t' : A$.
nodes.title: Subject reduction

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and terms $u$ and $t$, the term $t[k := u]$ is defined by recursion on $t$. For a variable, $\#i[k := u]$ is $\#i$ if $i < k$, is $u$ with every free variable raised by $k$ if $i = k$, and is $\#(i - 1)$ if $i > k$. A sort is unchanged, $(f\,a)[k := u] = f[k := u]\,a[k := u]$, $(\lambda (x : A).\, b)[k := u] = \lambda (x : A[k := u]).\, b[k + 1 := u]$, and…
nodes.title: Substitution for a de Bruijn variable

nodes.summary: A term is a variable $\#i$ with de Bruijn index $i \in \mathbb{N}$, a sort $s$ (either $\mathrm{Prop}$ or $\mathrm{Type}_i$ for some $i \in \mathbb{N}$), an application $f\,a$ of a term $f$ to a term $a$, an abstraction $\lambda (x : A).\, b$ with domain $A$ and body $b$, or a dependent product $\Pi (x : A).\, B$ with domain $A$ and codomain $B$.
nodes.title: Terms of the calculus of constructions

nodes.summary: Write $\bot$ for $\Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$. In the empty context, the application of the polymorphic identity $\lambda (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \lambda (x : A).\, x$ to $\bot$ has type $\Pi (x : \bot).\, \bot$.
nodes.title: Typing the polymorphic identity applied to falsity

nodes.summary: In the empty context, the polymorphic identity $\lambda (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \lambda (x : A).\, x$ has type $\Pi (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \Pi (x : A).\, A$.
nodes.title: Typing the polymorphic identity

nodes.summary: A context $\Gamma$ is a list of terms whose head is the type of the most recent variable; write $\Gamma, A$ for $\Gamma$ extended by $A$ at the head. The judgement $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ ($t$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$) is defined together with well-formedness of contexts as the least relation closed under the following rules.
nodes.title: Typing judgement of the calculus of constructions with universes

nodes.summary: A context is a list of terms whose head is the most recent binding. Well-formedness of contexts is defined together with the typing judgement $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ as the least predicate such that the empty context is well formed, and if $\Gamma$ is well formed and $\Gamma \vdash A : s$ for some sort $s$, then the context obtained from $\Gamma$ by adding $A$ at the head is well formed.
nodes.title: Well-formed contexts

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
